The fans went wild (Nigel Bacon had to be held down!) What a fine birthday present this was for their 'leader' Reg Hopkins. Vic Butcher improved on his best time for the 1000 metres Steeplechase with 3:02, only 2 seconds outside A.A.A.

Before Christmas 7 boys took part in a special 2 mile event which Vic Butcher won in a very powerful manner. In the under 21 5 miles Paul was narrowly beaten into second place while further back Andy turned the tables on Vic.
The Olympic Cup was won by Carl Lawton from a fast improving Paul Duckett. Andy Hinchcliff( who has six more years in this championship) revenged an earlier defeat by Vic Butcher to finish fourth.

Les Harris had one of his best runs to date to finish second on the opening stage, just eight seconds in arrears, but Vic Butcher was not at his best and had the misfortune to face Adams of West Surrey who raced away to record second fastest time of the day.

Vic Butcher did not produce one of his best runs in finishing 10th on the first stage but Bill Curtin, Peter Carton and John Stow all put in useful sub-12 efforts to gain us deserved third place medals.
Walton's Francis pipped Peter Carton again for third place and Tony Binda ran through strongly to secure 11th place, just two places ahead of Vic Butcher who closed in our scoring four.

Vic Butcher was to run the final leg that would normally have been Bill Curtin's. Vic is keen and dedicated to our club and sport and he trains hard and often, but he has yet to find the form we know he could produce.
